title: An autonomous four-dimensional quantum memory from a time-independent Toom Lindbladian
description: We prove exponential storage for the time-independent four-dimensional Toom dissipative toric code under any sufficiently weak additive finite-range Markovian Lindblad noise generator, including coherent Hamiltonian terms and non-unital dissipation such as amplitude damping. From an encoded start, a decoder reading only the current syndrome has worst-case fidelity at least 1 − C e^(−cL) at every 0 ≤ t ≤ e^(cL), in both CSS sectors and for all six logical qubits entangled with an untouched reference. The coherent threshold applies to the amplitude |h|, not h². For such additive noise this realizes the fully autonomous memory setting of Drechsler, Oreg and Aharonov, with translation invariance when the noise is homogeneous. The correction generator is exact; perturbations of its own jump operators and general non-Markovian baths remain open. Separate stochastic-Pauli theorems give explicit syndrome structure and allow spacetime local stochastic bounded-range multi-qubit and adaptive faults on unit time cells (one inverse correction rate), with a noise law independent of the logical input. On ℤ⁴, the independent-noise syndrome process has exponential component-diameter tails uniformly in time from empty syndrome. The corner convention is related to Pastawski, Clemente and Cirac's rule by x ↦ −x and a uniform X/Z relabelling. The general proof combines Poisson clearance and Toom contours with a coherent protected-region estimate, exact mixed differences and dense-set counting. The thresholds are non-explicit and astronomically small, and the size requirements are astronomically large.
